findings.title: Success path unconditionally closes breaker and clears other threads' probe flag
findings.evidence: After releasing the lock for the call, the success branch does 'self._state = self.CLOSED', 'self._failures = 0', 'self._opened_at = None' and 'self._probe_in_flight = False' (line 75) without checking whether the breaker was tripped or a probe was taken in the meantime.
findings.recommendation: Only apply the success transition if this call still owns the state it observed. Capture a generation counter (incremented on every state transition) under the lock before releasing it, and in the outcome handlers re-acquire the lock and bail out if the generation changed. At minimum, in the non-probing success case only reset '_failures'/'_opened_at' and never clear '_probe_in_flight' or overwrite OPEN/HALF_OPEN state set by another thread.

findings.title: Outcome handlers can undo an explicit reset() performed while a call is in flight
findings.evidence: The probe failure handler sets 'self._state = self.OPEN' and a fresh '_opened_at' unconditionally, even if reset() ran after the probe was admitted; the same applies to a stale CLOSED call failing at line 63.
findings.recommendation: Use the same generation/ownership check described above so a probe (or any in-flight call) that was admitted before reset() cannot re-open the breaker after the operator explicitly reset it.

findings.title: No timeout for a hung half-open probe leaves breaker wedged
findings.evidence: The probe flag is set with 'self._probe_in_flight = True' and only cleared by that same call's success or exception handlers; if the underlying call never returns (blocked socket, deadlock), the breaker stays HALF_OPEN with the probe flag set and every later call gets CircuitOpenError forever with no recovery except a manual reset().
findings.recommendation: Record the probe start time and treat an in-flight probe older than a configurable probe_timeout as expired inside _refresh_locked (clear the flag and allow a new probe), or document the wedging behaviour and require callers to wrap the probe in their own timeout.

findings.title: No tests for the single-probe half-open guarantee or the concurrent-success race
findings.evidence: The new module ships without tests; the behaviour guarded by 'raise CircuitOpenError("half-open probe in flight")' and the racy success path are exactly the parts that need deterministic coverage with a fake clock and threaded callers.
findings.recommendation: Add tests using the injectable clock: trip at threshold, verify rejection while OPEN, verify exactly one probe is admitted after reset_timeout, verify probe failure re-opens with a fresh cooldown, and add a concurrency test where a slow CLOSED-state call succeeds after another thread trips the breaker.
